standard.owner: QA (the head of quality assurance owns the standard; test-lab never edits it)
standard.drift: The standard has changed since this port. Each rule whose quoted text no longer appears is listed; re-port it before relying on that rule's findings.

rules.title: Specs import test and expect from fixtures/base.ts

source.quote: Extended test — import { test, expect } from here in every spec

check.how: Every *.spec.ts file imports `test` and `expect` from a module that resolves to fixtures/base, and neither from @playwright/test.

rules.title: No page objects constructed inside a spec

source.quote: never `new MyPage(page)` inside a spec body

check.how: No `new X(...)` in a spec where X is imported from the suite's pages/ folder or its name ends in Page.

rules.title: Locators are readonly properties assigned in the constructor, not getters

source.quote: Locators are **`readonly` properties assigned in the constructor** — never getter methods for parameterless locators.

check.how: In pages/ classes: a get accessor returning a locator, or a Locator-typed property without readonly, is a finding. Parameterized locator methods are allowed.

exceptions: Parameterized locators (methods that take an argument) stay as methods.

rules.title: No waitForTimeout

check.how: A call to waitForTimeout is a finding unless a comment directly above it, or on its line, explains why no event-driven wait is possible.

exceptions: If a timeout is unavoidable (e.g. debounce timer), add a comment explaining why no event-driven wait is possible.

rules.title: waitForFunction options are its third argument

source.quote: Always pass `null` explicitly as the arg when you only want to set options

check.how: waitForFunction(fn, { timeout | polling }) with exactly two arguments, the second an object literal of options, is a finding.

rules.title: Assertions retry on the locator, not on a value already read out

source.quote: **Always assert on `Locator`, never on resolved values** — web-first assertions auto-retry.

check.how: expect(await x.textContent()|innerText()|inputValue()|getAttribute()|isVisible()|isHidden()|isChecked()|isEnabled()|isDisabled()|count()|allTextContents()|allInnerTexts()), or expect(v) where v was assigned from one of those reads in the same function, is a finding. expect.poll is allowed.

exceptions: Parsed JSON-LD from page.evaluate() is unavoidably value-based; it is not a locator read and is not flagged.

check.how: A string or template literal containing [class*= is a finding.

rules.title: Every test title carries its case ID, @regression and a priority tag from the priority label

source.quote: Every test must include the TestRail case ID, priority tag, and `@regression`

check.how: Each test() title starts with a case ID (C<digits>, or a namespaced local ID for a developer addendum), and its tag list holds @regression and exactly one of @p1-@p4. With a corpus, the tag must equal the one the case's priority label maps to: the label number, never the priority_id ("2 - Short Regression", priority_id 3, maps to @p2); Undefined maps to @p3.

exceptions: Undefined priority is tagged @p3 with a one-line comment noting the default.

rules.title: Every skip or known failure has a COVERAGE-GAPS.md entry

source.quote: Every `test.skip()` in the suite must have a corresponding entry here — never a silent skip.

check.how: Each test.skip / test.fixme / test.fail inside, or declaring, a test whose title has a case ID needs that case number in COVERAGE-GAPS.md; test.fail also needs a reason string.

exceptions: The mobile viewport guard (`if ((page.viewportSize()?.width ?? 0) < 768) { test.skip(); return; }`) with a comment naming the companion coverage is the standard's own pattern, not a gap.

rules.title: playwright.config.ts follows the config baseline

check.how: testDir './tests', fullyParallel false, forbidOnly !!process.env.CI, retries process.env.CI ? 2 : 0, workers 1, timeout 60_000, expect.timeout 10_000, trace 'on-first-retry', screenshot 'only-on-failure', video 'retain-on-failure', actionTimeout 15_000, navigationTimeout 30_000. A different value directly under an explanatory comment is a documented deviation, not a finding.

exceptions: A value that differs from the baseline with an explanatory comment directly above it.

rules.title: The named browser projects are defined

source.quote: `desktop-firefox` and `tablet-ipad` are defined in every suite config like any other project.

check.how: projects names include desktop-chrome, desktop-safari, desktop-edge, mobile-iphone, mobile-android, desktop-firefox and tablet-ipad. Setup projects may be added. test-lab runs local Chromium only and reports the others as not run locally.

source.quote: Every suite under `automation/` must follow this layout:

check.how: fixtures/base.ts, pages/BasePage.ts, tests/, COVERAGE-GAPS.md and playwright.config.ts exist.

rules.title: QA's CI keeps retries: 2; a test-lab run always passes --retries=0, and a pass on retry is never a pass

check.how: Enforced by the run plan (src/run-plan.ts adds --retries=0 to every run and burn-in invocation and refuses any other retry count) and by the verdict (a retry pass is flaky: rule 5 or 6). Proven in tests/ts/verdict.test.ts ("phase 1: QA standard settlements") and tests/playwright/phase1.test.ts.

rules.title: A mobile viewport guard skip counts only when the case declares that configuration not applicable

source.quote: must include an explicit viewport guard so they skip on mobile projects instead of failing

check.how: With a corpus, a guarded test mapped to a case that declares a configuration narrower than the guard's width is a finding. In the verdict, a skip on a declared configuration is not a pass (rule 5); a result on an undeclared configuration is outside the verdict.

rules.title: test.fail specs never count toward ready

source.quote: the suite reports green as long as the test keeps failing for the expected reason

check.how: With a corpus, test.fail in a test mapped to a case is a finding. In the verdict an expected failure is never passed (rule 5 for a required case).

rules.title: Undefined priority is tagged @p3 but is never required

check.how: A regression case whose source priority was Undefined cannot be in the required set: the profile is invalid (rule 1) until QA assigns a priority or removes it.

rules.title: caseStep() and support/test-lab/ are a proposed change to QA's standard, not assumed

source.quote: POMs are exposed as **test fixtures** via `fixtures/base.ts`

check.how: Not checked. references/qa-standard-proposal.md is the proposal to QA. The checker never flags a spec for lacking caseStep(); the verdict needs it for the specs it governs.
